recipes.name: Smothered Chicken Breasts
ingredients_raw: 4 (6 ounce) skinless, boneless chicken breast halves

steps.text: Sprinkle chicken with salt and lemon pepper.

Heat oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Cook chicken breasts until no longer pink in the center and the juices run clear, 13 to 15 minutes. An instant-read thermometer inserted into the center should read at least 165 degrees F (74 degrees C). Remove and keep warm.

Place bacon in a large skillet and cook over medium-high heat, turning occasionally until evenly browned, about 10 minutes. Transfer bacon slices to a paper-towel-lined plate. Reserve 2 tablespoons drippings in the skillet. Add onion and brown sugar and cook, stirring occasionally until onion is golden, about 5 minutes.
Place two bacon strips on each chicken breast half, top with caramelized onions, and sprinkle with Colby-Monterey Jack cheese.

raw_recipe.headline: Smothered Chicken Breasts
raw_recipe.description: This satisfying, quick-cooking, one-skillet chicken dish combines crispy bacon, caramelized onions, and gooey shredded cheese; and clean-up is a breeze!

video.description: It’s chicken dinner night, and you can really wow them by smothering the chicken with delicious ingredients. First season chicken with lemon pepper and salt, then cook completely in your skillet. Fry up some bacon until crisp. Cook onion and brown sugar in bacon drippings—yum!—until softened and golden. Then top each breast with strips of bacon, caramelized onion and plenty of Colby-Monterey Jack cheese for a show-stopping entrée.

review.reviewBody: Im 14 my parents just started this diet only meat chicken turkey and veggies i cooked this up for them within 30 minutes one pan no hassle they LOVED it, so glad i could make them a nice dinner for two so simple yet so delicious (:

Made this tonight & I wish I had taken a picture! It was beautiful & delicious! I did things a little different. I didn't have any lemon pepper, and only has lime juice on hand. I looked up substitution recipes with lemon juice & just used lime juice in its place. Instead of measuring out each spice I just squeezed a little lime juice on each breast and sprinkled a little of each: granulated garlic & onion, s&p, and dried thyme leaves. I used vegetable oil, but next time I plan to use Avocado oil. I put a lid on the pan & cooked over med heat for 5 min each side. I used a separate pan & cooked the bacon while the chicken was cooking to save time. I followed the recipe for the onions, then layered the bacon, onions & cheese (I used Lucerne Fancy Cut - wide shred cheddar/jack mix) & I put it in my Ninja pro XL @ 450° for 5 min, topped w/a liile chopped parsley & wallah... Perfection!! Served w/steamed fresh cut green beans & Angel Hair Pasta & Parmesan. My husband loved it & so did I!!

I didn't have any brown sugar, so I used honey instead. I did not saute in the bacon grease to save many calories and a lot of fat, too. Rather, I wiped the pan with a paper towel for a second time, and sauted the onions and honey to a delicious brown. I made it a short time ahead, so I heated in the oven for 15 minutes at 350 to melt the cheese and blend the flavors Delicious!I will make again...

Really delicious. Like Jennifer Beigel suggestion, I baked mine. I precooked the bacon and the onions and then topped the chicken (thighs, not breasts) and baked at 425 for about 30 minutes. Really good. It's a keeper.

A simple, yet tasty recipe for chicken breasts. I am not a huge fan of chicken breasts as they tend to dry out and are less flavorful than legs/thighs. I didn't have all of the suggested ingredients, so I did improvise. I substituted cheddar cheese in place of colby-jack. And to finish, each breast was placed in an individual baking dish and placed under the broiler until the cheese started to brown. The finished dish turned out flavorful and the chicken did not dry out. I would recommend this recipe and will probably use this recipe again.

Pretty much followed the recipe except used half a chicken breast (lengthwise). I cooked the bacon in a skillet then just browned the chicken in the drippings....followed from there with crumbled bacon over the chicken topped with the onions and cheese mixture (Monte Jack with jalapeno). He really liked it. Prob will do again because it was easy and have ingredients on hand.

Family favorite. The second time I made it, I cut the bacon up, mixed it in the cheese & then sprinkled it all together - made cutting chicken easier when eating (no bacon to go thru). My MAIN RECOMMENDATION is to double the amount of onions you prepare - because they absolutely MAKE this dish.
Would have been better without all the brown sugar - maybe 1 TBSP - it was way too sugary sweet!

Quick, easy and so good! I didn’t have lemon pepper so I just used plain pepper. I added mushrooms to the onions to sauté and then I used Swiss cheese because that’s what I had on hand. I put it under the broiler just long enough to melt the cheese. Delish!!!

Wonderful. As people pointed out, cook the chicken however you like best. I browned the chicken in a cast iron pan then steam baked it for 25 minutes in our convection oven. Tender and moist. The toppings are the hit for this dish. I added mushrooms because we both like them. Delicious!

This was great. My husband loved it. The 2nd time I made it he wanted to try it as a sandwich, so I got some sandwich croissants and he said it was delicious. I did double the onion part, because we love onions. Definitely a repeat.
It was delicious!! I will be making it again

I’ve made this so many times now!! It’s in my regular rotation. Don’t be afraid to change up seasonings or cheeses or even different onions. It’s always yummy! I don’t use the brown sugar and don’t feel like it needs the sweetness. Thank you for this awesome and easy recipe! We love it!
Trying to double the recipe was interesting... ended up being good but I used less bacon and should have used less oil.
Have made this several times now as the family requests it. We serve with rice & a veg. Has a nice balance of sweet & savoury. Always a hit.

We thought this was good. I made one large breast for the two of us. I pounded it to a uniform thickness, and it was very tender cooking it for 5 minutes on a side. The brown sugar gave the onions a light sweetness. Everything is better with bacon! And a little cheese melted on top made it really good.
Added some mushrooms and peppers to the onions
Perfect! Wouldn't change anything this was delicious and my 4 year old loves it
